claim: RESOLFT microscopy relies on fluorophore switching between long-lived states.
source: The super-resolution microscopy called RESOLFT relying on fluorophore switching between longlived states, stands out by its coordinate-targeted sequential sample interrogation using low light levels.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a defining characteristic of RESOLFT microscopy.

claim: RESOLFT microscopy uses low light levels for coordinate-targeted sequential sample interrogation.
source: The super-resolution microscopy called RESOLFT relying on fluorophore switching between longlived states, stands out by its coordinate-targeted sequential sample interrogation using low light levels.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a distinguishing feature of RESOLFT.

claim: RESOLFT has been shown to discern nanostructures in living cells.
source: While RESOLFT has been shown to discern nanostructures in living cells, the reversibly photoswitchable green fluorescent protein (rsEGFP) employed in these experiments was switched rather slowly and recording lasted tens of minutes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as prior work.

claim: rsEGFP was switched rather slowly in previous RESOLFT experiments.

claim: Previous RESOLFT recordings using rsEGFP lasted tens of minutes.

claim: rsEGFP2 provides faster switching than rsEGFP.
source: We now report on the generation of rsEGFP2 providing faster switching and the use of this protein to demonstrate 25–250 times faster recordings.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: rsEGFP2 enables 25-250 times faster recordings than rsEGFP.

claim: For many decades lens-based optical microscopy could not resolve features finer than half the wavelength of light (λ/2 > 200 nm).
source: While for many decades lens-based optical microscopy could not resolve features finer than half the wavelength of light (λ/2 > 200 nm), the recent development of fluorescence nanoscopy or super-resolution imaging methods boosted its resolution potential (Hell, 2003, 2009; Huang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the historical context.

claim: Recent development of fluorescence nanoscopy or super-resolution imaging methods boosted the resolution potential of optical microscopy.
source: While for many decades lens-based optical microscopy could not resolve features finer than half the wavelength of light (λ/2 > 200 nm), the recent development of fluorescence nanoscopy or super-resolution imaging methods boosted its resolution potential (Hell, 2003, 2009; Huang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: In all super-resolution methods, the diffraction barrier is overcome by employing a fluorophore transition between two states.
source: In all these methods, the diffraction barrier is overcome by employing a fluorophore transition between two states, typically a fluorescent on- and a non-fluorescent off-state (Hell, 2009) in order to separate neighboring features.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: The fluorophore transition typically involves a fluorescent on-state and a non-fluorescent off-state.
source: In all these methods, the diffraction barrier is overcome by employing a fluorophore transition between two states, typically a fluorescent on- and a non-fluorescent off-state (Hell, 2009) in order to separate neighboring features.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: RESOLFT differs from stochastic single fluorophore on-off-switching methods by scanning a doughnut or line pattern across the sample.
source: The method called RESOLFT differs from stochastic single fluorophore on-off-switching methods by the fact that a doughnut or a line pattern is scanned across the sample, determining at any point in time the nanosized coordinate range where the fluorophores are in the on-state.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a distinguishing feature of RESOLFT.

claim: Using long lifetimes of the on- and off-states reduces the light intensities required for optical switching by orders of magnitude over the STED approach.
source: Using long lifetimes of the on- and off-states reduces the light intensities required for optical switching by orders of magnitude over the related STED approach, making RESOLFT attractive for extended live-cell or large area imaging.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an advantage of RESOLFT.

claim: RESOLFT is attractive for extended live-cell or large area imaging.
source: Using long lifetimes of the on- and off-states reduces the light intensities required for optical switching by orders of magnitude over the related STED approach, making RESOLFT attractive for extended live-cell or large area imaging.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a consequence of the low light requirements.

claim: RESOLFT was suggested almost a decade ago.

evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: The viability of RESOLFT was shown in principle by Hofmann et al., 2005; Dedecker et al., 2007; Schwentker et al., 2007.

claim: rsEGFP2 facilitates faster switching than rsEGFP.

claim: Replacing threonine 65 with alanine in EGFP transforms it into a fast switching RSFP with negative switching mode.
source: We observed that already the exchange of a single amino acid in the chromophore of the photostable and widely-used enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP) (Patterson et al., 1997; Tsien, 1998), namely replacing threonine 65 by alanine, transformed EGFP into a fast switching RSFP, which exhibited a 'negative switching mode'.

source: 'Negative switching' RSFPs switch from the on- into the off-state at the wavelength, here ~480 nm, that is used to elicit fluorescence.

claim: Switching from the off-state into the on-state in negative switching RSFPs is achieved by irradiation with ~405 nm light.
source: The switching from the off-state into the on-state is achieved by irradiation with a different wavelength, here ~405 nm.

claim: Protein solutions of EGFP(T65A) exhibited a high residual fluorescence (~50% of the on-state signal) when switched into the off-state.

claim: After the 20th image, the overall fluorescence of Vimentin-rsEGFP2 still amounted to 65% of its initial value.
source: After the 20th image, the overall fluorescence still amounted to 65% of its initial value, underscoring the bleaching resistance of rsEGFP2.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as an experimental result.

claim: The bleaching resistance of rsEGFP2 is underscored by the fact that after 20 images, the overall fluorescence still amounted to 65% of its initial value.
source: After the 20th image, the overall fluorescence still amounted to 65% of its initial value, underscoring the bleaching resistance of rsEGFP2.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: A resolution of <50 nm was achieved in raw image data of Keratin19-rsEGFP2 filaments.
source: Evaluating the intensity profiles of these filaments in the focal plane revealed a resolution <50 nm in raw image data (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The pixel dwell time for imaging the ER was cut down to 75 µs.
source: Next, we targeted rsEGFP2 to the lumen of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Since the ER is a fast moving structure we increased the recording speed further by doubling the light intensities (on: 405 nm, 4 kW/cm², 20 µs; off: 491 nm, 20 kW/cm², 50 µs; read-out: 491 nm, 76 kW/cm², 5 µs) thus cutting the pixel dwell time down to 75 µs, which is ~250 times faster than reported previously using rsEGFP.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as an experimental parameter.

claim: The pixel dwell time of 75 µs is ~250 times faster than reported previously using rsEGFP.
source: Next, we targeted rsEGFP2 to the lumen of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Since the ER is a fast moving structure we increased the recording speed further by doubling the light intensities (on: 405 nm, 4 kW/cm², 20 µs; off: 491 nm, 20 kW/cm², 50 µs; read-out: 491 nm, 76 kW/cm², 5 µs) thus cutting the pixel dwell time down to 75 µs, which is ~250 times faster than reported previously using rsEGFP.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a comparison.

claim: A field of 100 µm² was covered in 5.9 s for ER imaging.
source: Because we aimed at capturing fast movements, we also increased the pixel size to 40 nm × 40 nm, thus covering a field of 100 µm² in 5.9 s (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Repeated imaging revealed fast changes occurring in the range of seconds in the highly interconnected ER.
source: Repeated imaging revealed fast changes occurring in the range of seconds in the highly interconnected ER.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as an observation.

claim: A resolution of <90 nm was established in raw data for Keratin19-rsEGFP2 expressing cells using a similar dwell time as for ER imaging.
source: Since the ER-tubules are too large to determine the obtained resolution, we imaged again Keratin19-rsEGFP2 expressing cells using a similar dwell time and established <90 nm in raw data (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), meaning that speed was obtained at the expense of resolution.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Speed was obtained at the expense of resolution in the fast ER imaging experiments.
source: Since the ER-tubules are too large to determine the obtained resolution, we imaged again Keratin19-rsEGFP2 expressing cells using a similar dwell time and established <90 nm in raw data (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), meaning that speed was obtained at the expense of resolution.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as an interpretation.

claim: The movement of individual peroxisomes labeled with Pex16-rsEGFP2 was followed in the RESOLFT-mode in a 3 µm × 2 µm field of view at 2 Hz.
source: Likewise, when rsEGFP2 was fused to the protein Pex16 to highlight the peroxisomes in living PtK2 cells, we could follow the movement of individual peroxisomes in the RESOLFT-mode in a 3 µm × 2 µm field of view at 2 Hz (Figure 3E; Movie 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section and shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The overall photobleaching of rsEGFP2 was substantially lower than that of rsEGFP when fast RESOLFT imaging conditions were applied to peroxisomes.
source: Since the fluorescent proteins are confined to individual peroxisomes and do not diffuse over large distances, labeled peroxisomes are well suited for a direct comparison of rsEGFP2 and rsEGFP bleaching. The comparison showed that the overall photobleaching of rsEGFP2 was substantially lower than that of rsEGFP when the above fast RESOLFT imaging conditions were applied (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Phototoxicity is a major concern in (superresolution) fluorescence microscopy of living cells.
source: Phototoxicity is a major concern in (superresolution) fluorescence microscopy of living cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a general concern.

claim: STED-microscopy entails relatively large intensities (5-200 MW/cm2), depending on the desired resolution.
source: Among the established methods, STED-microscopy entails relatively large intensities, (5–200 MW/cm2), depending on the desired resolution.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a characteristic of STED.

claim: The wavelengths (560-800 nm) used for STED are in the comparatively benign long-wavelength part of the spectrum.
source: However, since the wavelengths (560–800 nm) used for STED are in the comparatively benign long-wavelength part of the spectrum (Hell, 2009), STED microscopy can image living cells and tissues, including neurons in the cerebral cortex of a living mouse (Berning et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section with citations.

claim: STED microscopy can image living cells and tissues, including neurons in the cerebral cortex of a living mouse.
source: However, since the wavelengths (560–800 nm) used for STED are in the comparatively benign long-wavelength part of the spectrum (Hell, 2009), STED microscopy can image living cells and tissues, including neurons in the cerebral cortex of a living mouse (Berning et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section with citations.

claim: In the RSFP-based RESOLFT microscopy demonstrated here, the employed light intensities (1-80 kW/cm2) are several orders of magnitude lower than in STED-microscopy.
source: In the RSFP-based RESOLFT microscopy demonstrated here, the employed light intensities (1–80 kW/cm2) are several orders of magnitude lower than in STED-microscopy and comparable to those used in live-cell confocal fluorescence microscopy.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a comparison.

claim: The light intensities employed in RSFP-based RESOLFT microscopy are comparable to those used in live-cell confocal fluorescence microscopy.
source: In the RSFP-based RESOLFT microscopy demonstrated here, the employed light intensities (1–80 kW/cm2) are several orders of magnitude lower than in STED-microscopy and comparable to those used in live-cell confocal fluorescence microscopy.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a comparison.

claim: Stochastic single-molecule based approaches typically use similar light intensities (0.1-100 kW/cm²) for imaging living cells.
source: Stochastic single-molecule based approaches, such as the methods called PALM (Manley et al., 2008; Shroff et al., 2008), STORM (Jones et al., 2011; Shim et al., 2012), and GSDIM (Fölling et al., 2008), typically use similar light intensities for imaging living cells (0.1–100 kW/cm² depending on the exposure time or camera frame rate), but they apply these intensities (i.e. temporal and spatial photon densities) continuously to all points in the imaged area.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section with citations.

claim: Stochastic single-molecule based approaches apply light intensities continuously to all points in the imaged area.
source: Stochastic single-molecule based approaches, such as the methods called PALM (Manley et al., 2008; Shroff et al., 2008), STORM (Jones et al., 2011; Shim et al., 2012), and GSDIM (Fölling et al., 2008), typically use similar light intensities for imaging living cells (0.1–100 kW/cm² depending on the exposure time or camera frame rate), but they apply these intensities (i.e. temporal and spatial photon densities) continuously to all points in the imaged area.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a characteristic of stochastic methods.

claim: In RESOLFT, any pixel is only illuminated during a small fraction of the recording time of the image.
source: Since our RESOLFT approach has been implemented as a point-scanning system, the intensities employed are applied only for a brief duration on a small, sub-micrometer sized region of the imaged area. Hence any pixel is only illuminated during a small fraction of the recording time of the image.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a characteristic of RESOLFT.

claim: In stochastic methods, the whole imaged area is irradiated for the entire time of recording.
source: In the stochastic methods, the whole imaged area is irradiated for the entire time of recording, that is for a couple of seconds or minutes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a characteristic of stochastic methods.

claim: In the RESOLFT microscopy demonstrated here, the total light dose impinging on the cell is lower by 3-4 orders of magnitude compared to the stochastic single-molecule based approaches.
source: Therefore, in the RESOLFT microscopy demonstrated here, the total light dose impinging on the cell is lower by 3–4 orders of magnitude compared to the stochastic single-molecule based approaches.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a comparison.

claim: For recording the shown RESOLFT images, 2-10 J/cm² were applied for switching into the on-state.
source: Concretely, for recording the shown RESOLFT images, 2–10 J/cm² were applied for switching into the on-state, and 25–300 J/cm² for eliciting fluorescence and switching the protein off.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as an experimental parameter.

claim: For recording the shown RESOLFT images, 25-300 J/cm² were applied for eliciting fluorescence and switching the protein off.
source: Concretely, for recording the shown RESOLFT images, 2–10 J/cm² were applied for switching into the on-state, and 25–300 J/cm² for eliciting fluorescence and switching the protein off.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as an experimental parameter.

claim: PALM live-cell imaging reportedly requires light doses of 1,000-100,000 J/cm² for on-switching with UV (405 nm) light.
source: PALM live-cell imaging reportedly requires light doses of 1,000–100,000 J/cm² for on-switching with UV (405 nm) light and 25,000–300,000 J/cm² for fluorescence excitation (Manley et al., 2008; Shroff et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section with citations.

claim: PALM live-cell imaging reportedly requires light doses of 25,000-300,000 J/cm² for fluorescence excitation.
source: PALM live-cell imaging reportedly requires light doses of 1,000–100,000 J/cm² for on-switching with UV (405 nm) light and 25,000–300,000 J/cm² for fluorescence excitation (Manley et al., 2008; Shroff et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section with citations.

claim: Live-cell GSDIM experiments using a yellow fluorescent protein required irradiation doses of 100,000-900,000 J/cm².
source: Live-cell GSDIM experiments using a yellow fluorescent protein required even larger irradiation doses (100,000–900,000 J/cm²) (Fölling et al., 2008; Testa et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section with citations.

claim: RESOLFT microscopy currently is the superresolution method entailing the lowest light dose.
source: Although RESOLFT microscopy may induce phototoxicity after extended exposure, similarly to live-cell confocal microscopy, it currently is the superresolution method entailing the lowest light dose.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a conclusion.

claim: RESOLFT microscopy has been used to image neurons in living organotypical hippocampal cultures over several hours without noticeable photodegradation.
source: Therefore, perhaps not surprisingly, RESOLFT microscopy has been used to image neurons in living organotypical hippocampal cultures over several hours without noticeable photodegradation (Testa et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section with a citation.

claim: The comparatively low-dose/low-intensity requirement of the RESOLFT concept is due to the fact that it uses long-lived on- and off-states.
source: Note that the comparatively low-dose/low-intensity requirement of the RESOLFT concept is due to the fact that it uses long-lived on- and off-states in combination with the fact that it does not require fast emission of many photons for establishing molecular coordinates (localization).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as an explanation.

claim: The RESOLFT concept does not require fast emission of many photons for establishing molecular coordinates (localization).
source: Note that the comparatively low-dose/low-intensity requirement of the RESOLFT concept is due to the fact that it uses long-lived on- and off-states in combination with the fact that it does not require fast emission of many photons for establishing molecular coordinates (localization).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as an explanation.

claim: The applied intensities in RESOLFT are largely determined by the on-off switching kinetics.
source: Since the applied intensities are largely determined by the on-off switching kinetics, the concept offers ample room for accommodating novel proteins with switching kinetics entailing even lower light doses and intensities.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as an explanation.

claim: The RESOLFT concept offers ample room for accommodating novel proteins with switching kinetics entailing even lower light doses and intensities.
source: Since the applied intensities are largely determined by the on-off switching kinetics, the concept offers ample room for accommodating novel proteins with switching kinetics entailing even lower light doses and intensities.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a speculation about future possibilities.

claim: rsEGFP2 is a bright, monomeric, photostable, quickly maturating, and fast switching alternative to rsEGFP with comparatively low photobleaching.
source: In conclusion, rsEGFP2 is a bright, monomeric, photostable, quickly maturating, and fast switching alternative to rsEGFP with comparatively low photobleaching.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a summary of rsEGFP2 properties.

claim: rsEGFP2 is expected to outperform other green fluorescent RSFPs because of its faster maturation and good usability for functional protein tagging.
source: We expect it to outperform other green fluorescent RSFPs (Ando et al., 2007; Stiel et al., 2007) because of its faster maturation and good usability for functional protein tagging.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section with citations as an expectation.

claim: An implementation of quick illumination sequences allowed up to 250-fold faster recordings as compared to previous reports.
source: An implementation of quick illumination sequences allowed us to realize up to 250-fold faster recordings as compared to previous reports, thus facilitating live-cell RESOLFT nanoscopy with pixel dwell times down to 70 µs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a main finding.

claim: Live-cell RESOLFT nanoscopy with pixel dwell times down to 70 µs was facilitated.
source: An implementation of quick illumination sequences allowed us to realize up to 250-fold faster recordings as compared to previous reports, thus facilitating live-cell RESOLFT nanoscopy with pixel dwell times down to 70 µs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a main finding.

claim: RESOLFT nanoscopy allows one to adapt speed and resolution within a certain range to the sample needs.
source: Since one can adjust both the duration and the illumination intensity, as well as the optical switching scheme, RESOLFT nanoscopy allows one to adapt speed and resolution within a certain range, to the sample needs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a characteristic of RESOLFT.

claim: In the point-scanning scheme used here, the total recording time of the image scales with the area of recording.
source: Finally, we note that in the point-scanning scheme used here, the total recording time of the image scales with the area of recording.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a characteristic of point-scanning.

claim: Parallelization of the scanning procedure with an array of doughnuts or lines overcomes the dependence on the field of view and cuts down the recording time by the degree of parallelization.
source: Parallelization of the scanning procedure with an array of doughnuts or lines (so-called 'structured illumination') (Gustafsson, 2005; Schwentker et al., 2007; Rego et al., 2012) overcomes this dependence on the field of view and cuts down the recording time by the degree of parallelization.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section with citations.

claim: Owing to the low-light level operation, the degree of parallelization can easily amount up to a factor of 100-1000.
source: Owing to the low-light level operation, the degree of parallelization can easily amount up to a factor of 100–1000.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a speculation about future possibilities.

claim: Given the short pixel dwell times attained, parallelized RESOLFT versions should enable video-rate nanoscopy across the whole field of view of the objective lens.
source: For this reason, given the short pixel dwell times attained herein, parallelized RESOLFT versions should enable video-rate nanoscopy across the whole field of view of the objective lens.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and discussion section as a speculation about future possibilities.
